reviewMethod: Direct inspection of rendered HTML screenshots and generated PNGs by Copilot

scope.designStatus: Enterprise foundation implemented and validated; not deployed

observations: Broker, worker, and LiteLLM Gateway are visibly separate Container Apps with independent replica ranges.
Node.js marks identify only the broker and worker runtimes; LiteLLM is a distinct gateway service.
Local tools and the upstream Copilot service remain outside the private workload boundary.
The worker carries only a per-user virtual key to LiteLLM; GitHub OAuth connections remain in the dedicated LiteLLM database.
Verified rich input, adaptive thinking, exact token counting, coordinated agent branches, compaction, Cron, automatic memory, background work and completed-turn resume are summarized.
Enterprise control PostgreSQL, LiteLLM PostgreSQL, and encrypted Blob checkpoints have separate state responsibilities.
No provisioning pipeline, IaC stage or deployment flow appears.
Both themes remain contained, with readable labels and conclusion cards at the largest desktop size.
The eight-stage main path crosses distinct approval, platform, onboarding and promotion lanes.
Failed acceptance goes to failure containment, never directly to production promotion.
Recovery requires an existing known-good release; the first-install and no-replay caveats are visible.
Bicep OR Terraform remains a mutually exclusive environment choice.
The workflow is explicitly proposed; no runtime inference topology is mixed into it.
Both themes fit the checked desktop sizes; the numbered raster storyboard is preferred for presentations.

presentationImages.correctedDefect: The poster now uses a light executive-presentation palette and smaller icons while preserving the shared inference-plane topology and exact storage relationships.
observations: The broker remains separate while worker and LiteLLM are grouped inside one shared inference-plane boundary.
Worker and LiteLLM remain separate Azure Container Apps with independent 2-30 and 2-10 replica ranges.
Warm off-white, white, and light blue-gray surfaces replace the prior dark full-card treatment.
Service and product icons are approximately 20-30 percent smaller so typography and topology lead the slide.
Muted Microsoft blue is reserved for request flow and hierarchy; amber remains limited to the limitations callout.
Node.js branding appears only on the broker and worker; the official LiteLLM logo identifies the gateway.
Encrypted Blob checkpoints remain a distinct branch-state service and are not collapsed into Enterprise PostgreSQL.
The LiteLLM database is explicitly limited to encrypted OAuth connections and gateway state.
Managed-identity, JWT trust, database and telemetry paths terminate at their intended components without crossing text.
The implemented/not-deployed badge is prominent and all production caveats remain readable.
The client remains unmodified with local tools; access remains per employee and entitled Claude model.
No native connector pool, APIM, VM, per-user container, shared seat, direct Anthropic credential or image-generation service appears.
The four governance lanes and failure-containment lane keep the eight-stage path readable.
Pass goes to staged rollout; Fail goes to Block promotion; If prior good goes only to Approved recovery.
The first-install block and prohibition on inference replay remain visible.
Bicep OR Terraform, federated identity and human authorization gates are preserved.
The proposed/not-implemented badge and existing single-user automation limitation are explicit.
No runtime inference graph is included; the small build/foundation notes remain readable at presentation size.

evidencePolicy: Automated delivery, screenshot and image-generation receipts are unchanged. Their pending visual-review fields are superseded only by this separate inspection record, not rewritten.
